styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Jamestown, Makola Market and live highlife.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Jollof, waakye and chop bars across the city.

styles.label: Beach
styles.blurb: Labadi and Bojo Beach plus a coastal drive.

stays.why: Walk to restaurants, bars and Oxford Street shops. Central for nightlife and easy taxi rides to the old town.
Closest to the airport and big hotels. Quiet streets, good for early flights and business trips.
Leafy and calm, with cafés and embassies nearby. A short ride from Osu and the beaches.
Quiet, upscale and central. Good for longer stays and travellers who want space and security.

food: Try Ghanaian staples: jollof rice, waakye (rice and beans), banku with tilapia, and fufu with light soup.
Chop bars are cheap local canteens. Expect a filling plate for roughly GHS 30–60; check the price first.
For red-red (beans, plantain and palm oil) and grilled tilapia, look around Osu and Labadi.
Street snacks: kelewele (spiced fried plantain), kebab skewers and roasted corn. Eat where it is busy and freshly cooked.
Book ahead for popular weekend spots. Many kitchens close early on Sundays; check on the day.
more_time: Add a day for Cape Coast and Elmina castles, about 2–3 hours west by road. Go early and hire a driver.
Swap one city day for Aburi Botanical Gardens and the hills, roughly an hour north of Accra.
Beach lovers can trade a city afternoon for Bojo Beach or a boat trip on the Volta near Ada.

recommend.why: Two nights covers Jamestown, Makola Market, the museums and a beach afternoon, with time left for Ghanaian food.

month_notes: Jan: Dry and warm, highs near 31°C. One of the best months to visit.
Feb: Still dry and warm, a few more showers. Good for sightseeing.
Mar: Warmer and wetter, about 13 rain days. Carry a light rain jacket.
Apr: Similar to March, around 14 rain days. Plan indoor sights for the afternoon.
May: The main rains arrive, about 21 rain days. Expect heavy downpours and traffic delays.
Jun: Wettest month, about 24 rain days. Pack rain gear and keep plans flexible.
Jul: Cooler at 27°C high but still wet, about 17 rain days. Short breaks of sun between showers.
Aug: Cool and damp, about 15 rain days. A small dry spell is possible; check on the day.
Sep: Rain returns, about 20 rain days. Allow extra time for flooded roads.
Oct: Wet, about 21 rain days. Good month for museums and food tours.
Nov: Rains ease to about 14 days. Comfortable and a good shoulder month.
Dec: Dry and warm, about 8 rain days. Busy and festive; book hotels early.

climate_guide.summary: Tropical and hot all year, around 27–31°C by day. A long rainy season runs roughly May to October.

items.title: Best time: December to February
items.text: Warm days near 31°C and the fewest rain days, about 4–8 a month. Ideal for walking and the beaches.

items.title: Rainy season May to October
items.text: Rain days peak at about 24 in June. Showers are often heavy but short; carry a rain jacket.

items.title: Hot and humid year-round
items.text: Lows stay around 23–25°C, so nights are warm. Light, breathable clothes work best.

items.title: Pack an umbrella
items.text: From May to October, expect wet afternoons. A compact umbrella and dry bag help.

items.title: Rain slows traffic
items.text: Heavy rain floods roads and jams traffic. Build extra time into taxi rides in the wet months.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light cotton clothes, sunscreen, a hat, mosquito repellent for evenings, and a light layer for air-conditioned rooms.

transit.best: Use Uber, Bolt or a taxi with the fare agreed first; TroTros are the cheap local option.

modes.text: No metro or tram in Accra. Don't plan around rail.
Minibuses are the main public transport. They run fixed routes and a 'mate' calls out destinations. Cheap but crowded.
Taxis rarely use meters, so agree the fare before you ride. Uber, Bolt, Yango and InDrive all work and are easy to book.
Hiring a car with a driver is common for sightseeing. Self-driving is possible but traffic is heavy.
Fine by day in areas like Osu. Watch for open drains and fast traffic; avoid unlit streets at night.
